properties.decision:
OPEN. `SPECIFIES` is currently NOT traversed by propagation. `nodes.rs` says so explicitly: "Structural edges not listed (e.g. SPECIFIES, DOCUMENTS, temporal bookkeeping) are intentionally not traversed."

THE ARGUMENT FOR TRAVERSING IT. It is grouped with DOCUMENTS, and the two are not alike. DOCUMENTS is human explanation — prose changing does not implicate the code. SPECIFIES is a MACHINE-READABLE CONTRACT: an OpenAPI file, a JSON schema, an IDL. When that changes, the implementation behind the interface may now be wrong, which is the definition of blast radius. Had SPECIFIES propagated and the edges been drawn, adding `Verification.description` to `schema/verify.yaml` would have lit up `ifc:mcp-tools` at the moment of the edit, which is exactly the miss that `req:declared-vocabulary-is-reachable-from-the-surface` exists for.

Direction would follow REALIZES, which has the same Artifact->target shape: forward Upstream, backward Downstream.

WHY IT IS NOT DECIDED NOW, and this is the substantive part rather than caution. It changes every blast radius in the graph, and it lands in the same window as two other changes that push the same dial the OTHER way:
  - `dec:the-default-scope-depth-should-be-two` SHRINKS regions (accepted, not yet built).
  - the future SE work adds subsystem interfaces, whose PROVIDES/CONSUMES edges ARE traversed and therefore GROW regions.
Turning all three at once means nobody can attribute the result. The sequence that stays measurable: land depth 2 and re-measure the 56-component sweep; then draw the SPECIFIES edges (which changes nothing while the edge is untraversed); then decide THIS with a before-and-after in hand.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: rerun the same instrument that produced `fact:defect-a-scoped-detector-at-its-default-depth-returns-two-thirds-of-the-design` with SPECIFIES traversable, and read what happens to the 50..60 spread. If regions stay discriminating, traverse it. If they do not, the contract relationship stays recorded-but-not-propagated, which is still strictly better than today's nothing.
properties.name: Whether a change to a contract artifact should reach the interface it specifies — measure after the depth change, do not decide ahead of it
properties.rationale:
RAISED BY ANTHONY'S QUESTION, 2026-08-17, which is what surfaced the whole thread: "in a system that builds a graph to represent relationships between two things, why is there no edge between these? it also sounds like some type of API contract."

The answer was that the edge exists, is defined for exactly this ("an OpenAPI / protobuf / JSON-schema / IDL file SPECIFIES an Interface (its authoritative contract)"), carries a `format` property listing `json_schema`, and has ZERO instances in the entire graph. It was written for INGEST — its `extraction_hint` is a prompt for pulling structure out of a user's documents — so it was built for other people's projects and never turned on this one. `rule:the-self-host-always-trails-what-it-teaches` is the right frame: the accurate reading is not "reflow2 failed to model itself" but "this is now catchable, for everyone".

An agent proposed and recommended nothing on this one at first pass and explicitly put it to the owner; the recommendation above (measure, do not decide) replaces that after the coupling was found.
